solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Seeing the future of a vicar only upset them initially (11)

indicators.note: the letters of A VICAR ONLY are knocked over into a new order
takes only the first letter of 'them'

blocks.note: first letter of 'them' joins the fodder

annotation.surface: A vicar gets flustered while claiming a glimpse of what lies ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seeing the future' is an adjective phrase here, just as CLAIRVOYANT is; 'upset' sits between the fodder and 'them initially', and the T goes into the mix too.
annotation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant person claims to see what has not yet happened.

entries.clue: US state exercise set up ancient weapons (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'set up' turns a word so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: CAL is the short form of California

annotation.walkthrough: Caltrops were small spiked iron pieces scattered on the ground to lame horses and foot soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: Caltrops are spiked devices used in warfare since Roman times.

entries.clue: Sprays also designed to protect painful back (8)

indicators.note: the letters of ALSO are arranged afresh
the rearranged ALSO wraps round the other piece
'back' as in going back: the word runs in the opposite direction, so SORE becomes EROS

annotation.surface: An advert for spray cans built to shield a bad back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Painful back' reads as a complaint in the surface; here 'back' is an instruction applied to SORE.
annotation.definitionFit: Aerosols are cans that release their contents as a spray.

entries.clue: Figure house doctor should support Republican (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports sits underneath, so HO + MB go below R

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

annotation.surface: A house doctor backing a Republican politician.
annotation.walkthrough: A RHOMB (rhombus) is a four-sided figure with all sides equal.
annotation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a geometric figure, a parallelogram with equal sides.

entries.clue: Reserved and rode off looking embarrassed (7)

indicators.note: RODE goes off, i.e. goes wrong and comes out in a new order

annotation.surface: A shy rider leaves with a flushed face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' reads as shy, but it means booked ahead, as a table or a book can be ordered.
annotation.definitionFit: To order a thing in advance is to reserve it.

entries.clue: Tested when on top of state education (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, AS sits above SAY + ED

annotation.surface: Pupils are examined as they arrive at the top level of state schooling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State education' reads as one phrase about schools; it splits into a verb, SAY, and an abbreviation, ED.
annotation.definitionFit: To assay a metal or ore is to test its purity.

entries.clue: Tasty — to an unspecified number eating hot stew (9)

indicators.note: TO SOME takes the other piece inside it
the letters of HOT are stewed into a new order

annotation.surface: A recommendation of a hot stew served to a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the dish being eaten; it is the instruction to mix up HOT. 'Eating' works on the phrase TO SOME as one unit.
annotation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is pleasant to eat.

entries.clue: Cold shoulder — of lamb? (3)

blocks.note: to give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them deliberately
a shoulder of lamb is one joint a butcher sells; the question mark says it is an example

annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoulder' does double duty: with 'Cold' it is a snub, with 'of lamb' it is a joint of meat; the question mark flags the example.
annotation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them pointedly, and a shoulder of lamb is a butcher's cut.

entries.clue: Cougars will accept he does (6)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so CATS takes HE into its middle

annotation.surface: Older women will take a man, as he knows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Does' is the verb 'do' as in 'do someone out of money', not a plural of doe or a helper verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, so does means cheats.

entries.clue: Easily irritated, one leaves the City in turmoil (6)

indicators.note: one who leaves departs, so the I (one) departs from THE CITY
the remaining letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: THE CITY without its I, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A grumpy banker quits the chaotic financial district.
annotation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, which suits an FT surface; here it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable, quick to take offence.

entries.clue: Slow student has a right turn (5)

annotation.surface: A slow learner takes the right-hand turn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slow student' reads as one phrase; 'Slow' alone is the definition, the musical tempo marking.
annotation.definitionFit: Largo is the Italian musical direction for a slow, broad tempo.

entries.clue: Bent receiver must have one way (9)

annotation.surface: A crooked receiver of stolen goods needs an escape route.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a fence handling stolen goods, which fits 'Bent'; it is a satellite dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for crooked or corrupt.

entries.clue: Scrape by, accepting blunder could be a show of contempt (9)

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so BY takes ERR between its letters

annotation.surface: Someone just scraping by makes an error that earns scorn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrape by' reads as one phrase meaning to just manage; the two words do separate jobs, and 'by' is used as it stands.
annotation.definitionFit: A raspberry is the rude noise blown with the tongue out, a show of contempt.

entries.clue: Minor problem with answer for one opening (5)

indicators.note: A goes in for I, replacing it

blocks.note: a hitch is a small snag
one = I, the letter swapped out

annotation.surface: A snag with an answer for someone's opening.
annotation.walkthrough: HITCH with its I (one) replaced by A (answer) gives HATCH.
annotation.definitionFit: A hatch is an opening in a deck, floor or wall.

entries.clue: Kept control of parasites in whales (7)

indicators.note: parasites living in whales sit inside them, so LICE sits inside POD

blocks.note: a pod is a group of whales

annotation.surface: Someone controlled the parasites living on whales.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whales' is a collective clue: a group of whales is a POD.
annotation.definitionFit: To police something is to keep it under control.

entries.clue: Pass poor dosser getting such blisters (4,5)

indicators.note: DOSSER is in poor shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass

annotation.surface: A homeless man sleeping rough ends up with blisters.
annotation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for someone sleeping rough. 'Such' points the definition back at the clue: the dosser in the scene gets cold sores.
annotation.definitionFit: Cold sores are blisters round the mouth caused by a herpes virus.

entries.clue: Low returns on diamonds must mean inevitable ruin (4)

indicators.note: what returns comes back the way it went, so MOO runs the other way
in an across clue, OOM comes after D

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do; MOO reversed

annotation.surface: A bridge player's poor returns on diamonds spell certain disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low returns' reads as poor profits; 'Low' is the cow's MOO.
annotation.definitionFit: Doom is a fate of ruin that cannot be escaped.

entries.clue: British Rail originally invested in new toilet book (8)

indicators.note: takes the first letters of British Rail
BR is put inside the other piece
TOILET is made new, its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: British Rail has paid for a new station toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book' is the text of an opera or musical, which is what a libretto is.
annotation.definitionFit: The book of a musical or opera is its libretto, the words as opposed to the score.

entries.clue: Advance making progress on the backs of others (8)

definitions.note: the second definition describes the game rather than naming it

definitions.text: making progress on the backs of others

blocks.note: a verb: to jump ahead of rivals, skipping stages

blocks.clueFragment: making progress on the backs of others
blocks.note: the children's game of vaulting over bent backs

annotation.surface: A career climber gets ahead by using other people.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a sneer at an exploiter; taken literally it is the playground game.
annotation.definitionFit: To leapfrog is to advance past others, and in the game you literally progress over their backs.

entries.clue: A final cut short, unfortunately (4)

indicators.note: LAST loses its final letter

annotation.surface: A cup final sadly ended early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Final' is an adjective here, LAST, rather than a match.
annotation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, like unfortunately.

entries.clue: Student son’s arrest reported (7)

indicators.note: what is said is heard as another word

blocks.note: S = son, and a collar is an arrest

annotation.surface: A student's son has been arrested, according to the news.
annotation.walkthrough: COLLAR is police slang for an arrest; S + COLLAR said together sounds like SCHOLAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A scholar is a student, especially one holding a scholarship.

entries.clue: Viceroy, king and ambassador in front of disreputable club (7)

blocks.note: HE, His Excellency, an ambassador's title
a dive is a seedy bar or club

annotation.surface: Grand officials heading to a seedy nightclub.
annotation.walkthrough: The Khedive was the Ottoman sultan's viceroy ruling Egypt.
annotation.definitionFit: Khedive was the title of the viceroy of Egypt under Ottoman rule.

entries.clue: Family doctor at home is number one in team (7)

annotation.surface: The family doctor who stays at home is the star of the side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one GP; 'Family' is KIN and 'doctor' is GP.
annotation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in a group.

entries.clue: Discourage study covering a politician (6)

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around something, so DEN wraps around A MP

annotation.surface: Research into a politician puts people off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb; it is a room, a DEN.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: wetting a fire makes it burn less, just as discouragement makes enthusiasm burn less.

entries.clue: Drop it off , being sluggish (6)

indicators.note: DROP IT goes off, its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A command to stop something, since it has become slow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop it off' reads as a delivery instruction; 'off' is what scrambles DROP IT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Latin for numb; hibernating animals are described as torpid.

entries.clue: A cat’s tiny bits (5)

blocks.note: TOM'S, a tom being a male cat

annotation.surface: A cat's toys or scraps.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe carries across: a cat's becomes a tom's, and the apostrophe is dropped in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose everyday sense: an atom once meant the smallest indivisible bit, as in 'not an atom of truth'.

entries.clue: Polish group rejected seductive scheme (5,4)

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so PARTY runs backwards

blocks.note: to hone is to polish or sharpen

annotation.surface: A Polish faction turned down a plan to seduce.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is the verb, to polish or HONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A honey trap is a scheme using seduction to compromise someone.

entries.clue: Plant seen in your cocoa, intermittently (5)

indicators.note: something intermittent stops and starts, so letters are taken, skipped, taken, skipped

annotation.surface: Something growing in your hot drink now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seen in' tempts a hidden-word hunt, but no run of five letters works; the letters are spaced out through both words.
annotation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant of the Americas.

entries.clue: FT magazine article found in office? (5,4)

blocks.note: the FT, Financial Times, is a newspaper
the magazine of a gun, holding cartridges

annotation.surface: A feature in the FT's weekend magazine about office life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' sits beside FT to look like its weekend supplement; it is an ammunition clip. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A paper clip is a small item typically found in an office.

entries.clue: Supply food for a disheartened type in credit (5)

indicators.note: TYPE loses its heart, leaving T…E
a person in credit is held within it, so A TE sits inside CR

blocks.note: TYPE with its middle YP removed

annotation.surface: A downcast person, living on credit, is fed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' looks like mood; it means the middle letters are removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the caterer's trade; the wider sense of catering to any need grew from it.

entries.clue: Show agreement, backing academic type (3)

indicators.note: backing is moving backwards, as a car backs up, so DON runs in reverse

blocks.note: a don is an Oxford or Cambridge lecturer

annotation.surface: Someone gives assent, supporting a university professor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support; it means reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb for a gesture: dipping the head is the usual silent sign of yes.

entries.clue: Offer false hope to new girl’s agent on lacking energy (6,5)

indicators.note: the letters are made new, rearranged
AGENT ON goes without the E

annotation.surface: A talent agent gives a new girl empty promises.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator 'new' comes first and covers the whole fodder, including AGENT ON once E is gone.
annotation.definitionFit: To string someone along is to keep them hoping with no intention of delivering.
